I've worked out all eight answers and saved them to `answer.json`. I checked a, b and g a second way with plain SQL and got the same numbers.

```json
{"a_segment": "smb", "a_net": 297014574, "b_customers": 249, "c_category": "sw", "c_net": 236742362, "d_month": "2025-08", "e_email": "u121@ex.com", "f_repeat": 232, "g_avg": 677688, "h_growth": -8.8}
```

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest Q3 net sales | smb, 297,014,574원 (enterprise 280,372,726 / consumer 250,070,797) |
| b. Customers with a paid Q3 order | 249 people |
| c. Category with the highest Q3 net sales | sw, 236,742,362원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 (291,379,959원) |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refunds | u121@ex.com (2,031,255원, no tie) |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid Q3 orders | 232 people |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 677,688원 (1,221 orders) |
| h. Change from August to September | −8.8% (265,808,603 vs 291,379,959, i.e. −8.776%) |

**What I found in the data:**
- **Segment names:** the same segment was written several ways, such as `" consumer"`, `"Enterprise "` and `"SMB"`. After trimming spaces and lowercasing, they collapse into three: smb, enterprise and consumer.
- **Duplicate emails:** the 300 customer accounts belong to 250 distinct emails. b, e and f count by email.
- **KST vs UTC:** 101 paid orders change quarter depending on whether you use UTC or KST, so the time zone conversion matters. All date checks use UTC+9.
- **No integrity problems:** every refund has a matching order line, and no refund quantity exceeds the quantity ordered.

**Decision for you:** some people who share one email have accounts in different segments. For example, u101 has one consumer account and one smb account. For a, I counted each order under the segment of the account that placed it. If you'd rather assign each person a single segment, the total for a could change.
